question: The autobiography ‘Long Walk to Freedom’ is written by:
solution:
The correct answer is __Nelson Mandela__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Long Walk to Freedom** is an autobiographical work written by South African President Nelson Mandela and was **first published in 1994.**
 
• **Nelson Mandela** was a** South African political leader. **
 
• He is well known as the father of the nation of South Africa.
 
• He is well known for the Anti-Apartheid Movement in South Africa.
 
• He served as the first President of South Africa from 1994 to 1999.
 
• India awarded him the Bharat Ratna in 1990.
 
• Pakistan awarded him Nishan-e-Pakistan in 1992.
 
• Honoured with the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.
 
• Notable works: 
 
 
• Conversations With Myself.
 
• The Struggle Is My Life.
 
• No Easy Walk to Freedom.
 
• In His Own Words.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• BR Ambedkar

 
 
• ​Dr. BR Ambedkar was elected to the constituent assembly from West Bengal.
 
• The Constituent Assembly of India was elected to draft the Constitution of India.
 
• An idea for a Constituent Assembly was first proposed in 1934 by M. N. Roy.
 
• It became an official demand of the Indian National Congress in 1935.
 
 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore 
 
 
• It was born on 7th May 1861 in the Bengali Brahim family. 
 
• He was the first non-European and first from Asia who was conferred with the Nobel Prize in Literature for the extraordinary "Gitanjali" in 1913.
 
• Satyendranath Tagore(Elder brother) of Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian who passed the elite Indian Civil Services examination from India.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore founded the famous Visha-Bharati(Santiniketan) in 1917.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**
 
 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, commonly known as Mahatma Gandhi, was an Indian lawyer, politician and national who promoted and practised nonviolent resistance to lead the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule.
 
• During his lifetime, Gandhiji ran four publications — Indian Opinion, Young India, Navajeevan and Harijan.
 
• Among his other noteworthy books are Hind Swaraj or Indian Home Rule, Satyagraha in South Africa, etc.
